content.text:
Finding submitted: **deviation** on the assignment provisions.

- **Section 20(d)** (p0142) bars either party from assigning without the other's consent — no successor/M&A carve-out and no reasonableness standard.
- **Section 3(c)** (p0033) independently prohibits Sparkling from assigning at all absent Garman's written authorization, which is squarely in walk-away territory (blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out).
- **Section 17** contains no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right, so no cure was required there.

Redline targets the fallback: either party may assign to a successor to its business or assets on written notice; any other assignment requires consent not to be unreasonably withheld; and Section 3(c) is conformed by a minimal carve-out so it no longer contradicts the new right.
